facts.claim: Top-quartile consumer apps hold 25% to 40% at day 30 and their curves flatten between day 60 and day 90
facts.excerpt: Top-quartile consumer apps see Day 30 retention of 25 to 40 percent and flatten by Day 60 to 90.

facts.claim: The mobile day-30 average runs 7% to 8%, with strong products above 15%
facts.source_title: The complete guide to measuring user retention
facts.excerpt: Mobile benchmark for Day 30 is 7-8% average, 15%+ for strong products.

facts.claim: SaaS subscription products often reach 40% to 50% day-30 retention, several times the mobile average
facts.source_title: The complete guide to measuring user retention
facts.excerpt: SaaS subscription products often hit 40-50% Day 30 retention.

facts.claim: Fintech apps retain a median 28% at day 1, 12% at day 7 and 7% at day 30, with strong performers at 35-45%, 18-25% and 10-15%
facts.source_title: App Retention Benchmarks: How Your App Stacks Up by Industry
facts.excerpt: Fintech apps: strong performers 35-45% Day-1, 18-25% Day-7, 10-15% Day-30; medians 28%, 12% and 7%.

facts.claim: Gaming apps retain a median 32% at day 1, 8% at day 7 and 3% at day 30, with strong performers at 40-50%, 12-18% and 5-8%
facts.source_title: App Retention Benchmarks: How Your App Stacks Up by Industry
facts.excerpt: Gaming apps: strong performers 40-50% Day-1, 12-18% Day-7, 5-8% Day-30; medians 32%, 8% and 3%.

facts.claim: E-commerce and retail apps retain 3% to 6% by day 30, above the 2% median other sources report for the same category
facts.source_title: Retention rates for mobile apps by industry
facts.excerpt: By Day 30, e-commerce or retail apps retain 3-6%.

facts.claim: About half of users who ever pay do so within two days of installing, and 90% within two weeks
facts.source_title: Install-to-first-revenue timing: mobile app payback windows in 2026
facts.excerpt: Roughly half of revenue-converting users do so within two days of install, and 90% convert within two weeks.

contradictions: Published day-30 retention for e-commerce does not agree: appstorys.com gives 3% to 6% while enable3.io reports a 2% median for the same category. Neither states which apps entered the sample or whether the figure is a mean or a median. Both appear on this page.
